answer: Give every agent a vertex in a public work graph: each epoch, a random subset of agents is audited by peers drawn from a disjoint slice of the graph, like branches of a juniper that never touch. An audited agent must show the atlas of its recent work — receipts, counterparties, outcomes — and peers stake a small bond on the verdict. A Sybil farm must fake a full atlas for every identity and survive audits on each one, so its cost scales linearly with the number of fake identities while an honest agent pays one audit per epoch. Failing an audit burns the bond and prunes the vertex.
